assignment: Scope: core (as defined in the brief), including the expressions section. PL/pgSQL bodies are dollar-quoted strings the server parses later, so probe CREATE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE forms (LANGUAGE, RETURNS TABLE/SETOF, volatility, SECURITY DEFINER, SET, PARALLEL, SQL-standard BEGIN ATOMIC bodies, RETURN expr) rather than PL/pgSQL statements. Query syntax includes DISTINCT ON, LATERAL, TABLESAMPLE, ROWS FROM, WITH ORDINALITY, GROUPING SETS/CUBE/ROLLUP, FILTER, WINDOW clause and frame exclusion, FOR UPDATE/SHARE/NO KEY UPDATE/KEY SHARE with NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED, FETCH ... WITH TIES, recursive CTE SEARCH/CYCLE, MATERIALIZED CTEs, data-modifying CTEs, INSERT ON CONFLICT, RETURNING, MERGE (incl. RETURNING and WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE), JSON_TABLE, array/composite/range literals. Engine: PostgreSQL 17. Doc entry points: SQL commands https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-commands.html ; SELECT https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-select.html ; lexical structure https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-syntax-lexical.html ; value expressions https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-expressions.html ; functions https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/functions.html ; data types https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/datatype.html . pglast (the real PostgreSQL parser) is a reliable reference: a probe pglast rejects is almost certainly invalid SQL.

Scope: core (as defined in the brief), including the expressions section. Include compound statements in stored programs (BEGIN...END, DECLARE variables/conditions/handlers/cursors, SET, IF, CASE, LOOP, REPEAT, WHILE, LEAVE, ITERATE, RETURN, OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE, SIGNAL/RESIGNAL, GET DIAGNOSTICS). Query syntax includes index hints, STRAIGHT_JOIN, optimizer hints /*+ */, LIMIT offset,count, FOR UPDATE/SHARE NOWAIT/SKIP LOCKED, INTO OUTFILE/DUMPFILE/@vars, WITH ROLLUP, window functions, LATERAL derived tables, JSON_TABLE, TABLE and VALUES statements, INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE / IGNORE / SET form / row alias, REPLACE, multi-table UPDATE/DELETE, partition selection, user variables (@x, @@global.x). Engine: MySQL 8.4. Doc entry points: SQL statements https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/sql-statements.html ; SELECT https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/select.html ; compound statements https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/sql-compound-statements.html ; language structure https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/language-structure.html ; functions https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/functions.html ; data types https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/data-types.html . The mysql client's DELIMITER command isn't SQL; don't use it in probes.

Scope: core (as defined in the brief), including the expressions section. Include T-SQL's procedural language: BEGIN...END, DECLARE @var, SET/SELECT assignment, IF...ELSE, WHILE, BREAK/CONTINUE, GOTO, RETURN, TRY...CATCH, THROW, RAISERROR, WAITFOR, PRINT, cursors (DECLARE/OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE/DEALLOCATE), table variables, temp tables, and the GO batch separator. Query syntax includes TOP, OUTPUT, APPLY, PIVOT/UNPIVOT, TABLESAMPLE, table and query hints, FOR XML/JSON, OFFSET/FETCH. Engine: SQL Server 2022 / Azure SQL Database. Doc entry points: statements index https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/statements ; queries https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/queries/queries ; language elements https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/language-elements/language-elements-transact-sql ; data types https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/data-types/data-types-transact-sql . Tip: the same docs are markdown at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/sql-docs/live/docs/t-sql/<section>/<page>.md (e.g. statements/create-table-transact-sql.md, queries/select-transact-sql.md), much easier to read with curl.

Scope: core (as defined in the brief), including the expressions section. Include PL/SQL as it appears in SQL scripts: anonymous blocks (DECLARE/BEGIN/EXCEPTION/END), declarations, %TYPE/%ROWTYPE, assignment, procedure calls, IF/CASE, LOOP/WHILE/FOR (numeric and cursor), EXIT/CONTINUE, cursors, REF CURSOR/OPEN FOR, BULK COLLECT, FORALL, RETURNING INTO, EXECUTE IMMEDIATE, RAISE and exception handlers, collections and records, and the SQL*Plus `/` line that ends a PL/SQL unit in scripts. Query syntax includes CONNECT BY, MODEL, PIVOT/UNPIVOT, flashback AS OF, SAMPLE, OFFSET/FETCH, MATCH_RECOGNIZE, (+) outer joins, multitable INSERT ALL/FIRST, DML error logging. Other SQL*Plus commands (SET SERVEROUTPUT, SPOOL, @script) are not in the SQL index; don't add them. Engine: Oracle AI Database 26ai (docs path /23/ redirects to /26/; use whichever the site serves). Doc entry points: SQL statements index https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/23/sqlrf/Types-of-SQL-Statements.html ; SQL Language Reference https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/23/sqlrf/ ; PL/SQL Language Reference https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/23/lnpls/ .

Scope: core (as defined in the brief), including the expressions section. Include Snowflake Scripting (blocks, DECLARE, LET, IF/CASE, FOR/WHILE/REPEAT/LOOP, EXCEPTION, cursors, RESULTSET, RETURN). Query syntax includes semi-structured access (col:a.b[0]), :: casts, time travel AT/BEFORE, CHANGES, MATCH_RECOGNIZE, PIVOT/UNPIVOT, SAMPLE, LATERAL FLATTEN, CONNECT BY, QUALIFY, ASOF JOIN. Engine: Snowflake (current docs). Doc entry point: all commands https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql-all (each command links to its page). Also: query syntax https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/constructs ; scripting https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/snowflake-scripting/index ; operators https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/operators ; data types https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/intro-summary-data-types .

Scope: everything: every statement in the vendor's statement index, plus the expressions section (use the brief's core list to decide which statements need full clause depth). Doc entry points: https://www.sqlite.org/lang.html (every statement and its syntax diagram), expressions https://www.sqlite.org/lang_expr.html , keywords https://www.sqlite.org/lang_keywords.html , PRAGMA https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html (one entry for PRAGMA with its forms; individual pragma names don't need entries).

Scope: core (as defined in the brief), including the expressions section. Scope: core (as defined in the brief), including the expressions section. Scope: "rest": every statement in the vendor's statement index that isn't in the brief's core list. No expressions section. That's about 150 of the 183 SQL commands (aggregates, casts, collations, domains, event triggers, extensions, FDW objects, operators, policies, publications, roles, rules, sequences, statistics, subscriptions, tablespaces, text search, triggers, types, user mappings; ANALYZE, CALL, CHECKPOINT, CLUSTER, COMMENT, COPY, cursors, DISCARD, DO, LISTEN/NOTIFY, LOCK, PREPARE/EXECUTE, REINDEX, REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, SET/RESET/SHOW, VACUUM, ...). COPY is high tier and needs depth (FROM/TO, STDIN/STDOUT/PROGRAM, query source, WITH options, legacy options). Engine: PostgreSQL 17. Doc entry points: SQL commands https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-commands.html ; SELECT https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-select.html ; lexical structure https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-syntax-lexical.html ; value expressions https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-expressions.html ; functions https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/functions.html ; data types https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/datatype.html . pglast (the real PostgreSQL parser) is a reliable reference: a probe pglast rejects is almost certainly invalid SQL.

Scope: "rest": every statement in the vendor's statement index that isn't in the brief's core list. No expressions section. Includes events, triggers, servers, tablespaces, logfile groups, spatial reference systems, resource groups, users and roles; CALL, DO, HANDLER, IMPORT TABLE, LOAD DATA, LOAD XML, LOCK/UNLOCK TABLES, XA, PREPARE/EXECUTE/DEALLOCATE, replication and group replication statements, account management, table maintenance (ANALYZE/CHECK/CHECKSUM/OPTIMIZE/REPAIR TABLE), INSTALL/UNINSTALL, CLONE, SET variants, every SHOW statement, BINLOG, CACHE INDEX, FLUSH, KILL, LOAD INDEX INTO CACHE, RESET, RESTART, SHUTDOWN, DESCRIBE, HELP, USE. Dialect `base` is the strict ISO/IEC 9075 (SQL:2016/2023) base grammar, not a vendor engine. Scope: every SQL-statement production of ISO 9075-2 Foundation (the <SQL procedure statement> family: schema definition and manipulation, data manipulation, transaction, connection, session, diagnostics, dynamic SQL, and SQL/PSM control statements if you include Part 4), plus the expressions section (every <value expression>, <predicate>, literal and type form), using the Core features (E/F/T codes marked Core) for tier high and optional features for medium/low. Doc entry points: the SQL:2016 Foundation BNF https://jakewheat.github.io/sql-overview/sql-2016-foundation-grammar.html (use its #anchors as doc: URLs), and the feature list with Core marking https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/features-sql-standard.html and https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/unsupported-features-sql-standard.html . Set engine: "ISO SQL", version: "SQL:2016". Embedded-SQL host constructs are `not-sql`. Probes must be valid ISO SQL; no vendor syntax.
